messages:
Ashley M: Heads up — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spikes since ~02:00 UTC. Escalation from support: ticket #CUST-2345. Initial correlation looks like the driver/kernel maintenance we rolled at 00:45 UTC on the eu-west pool. Can infra take a look?

Diego R: I see it. Grafana p95 for text-gen endpoints jumped from ~220ms to ~900ms and p99 from ~780ms to ~2.3s across nodes in eu-west-2. Throughput stable.

Maria S: Customer-facing note: we told them we were investigating and to expect updates.

Diego R: Quick repro: call same prompt repeatedly against a dedicated instance on node node-euw2-14. p99s are horrible. I grabbed a few samples and ran basic host checks. Sharing outputs inline.

Diego R: ```
ssh ubuntu@node-euw2-14
uname -a
Linux redwood-node-14 6.1.0-rc1 #1 SMP PREEMPT Wed Mar 11 23:21:12 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv
Driver Version, Name, Utilization, Memory Used
535.54, A100-SXM-80GB, 12 %, 18 GiB
```

Diego R: iostat and vmstat show IO wait intermittently spiking while p99s spike.

Diego R: ```
vmstat 1 6
procs -----------memory---------- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ------cpu-----
 r  b   swpd   free   buff  cache   si   so    bi    bo   in   cs us sy id wa st
 2  0      0  102400  31224  512000    0    0  1200  9800  320  430 10  8 60 22  0
 1  0      0  101900  31220  512500    0    0  4000 42000  160  210 12 10 52 26  0
```

Diego R: iostat -x shows high await on nvme0n1 during the spike windows (200-600ms).

Noah P: Interesting — GPU driver 535.54 was rolled in the maintenance. We previously had 525.x. I'll search the driver changelog for anything about page-fault handling or DMA that could affect NVMe I/O.

Tess L: Also saw repeated "NVRM: Xid" messages in dmesg on some nodes around the same time. Pasting snippets.

Tess L: ```
[  1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  1234.568012] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
```

Diego R: That aligns with customer reports — intermittent stalls when batch workloads hit >80% concurrency. Looks like the kernel is getting blocked waiting on NVMe while GPUs trigger page-fault/DMA ops.

Ashley M: @Noah P can you escalate to NVIDIA with logs (dmesg, nvidia-smi, iostat) and ask about 535.x + Linux 6.1 interaction? Also we need a mitigations plan for affected customers.

Noah P: Already opened SR with NVIDIA. Attaching case ref: NV-2026-8472. Sent logs and sample pcap + perf counters. They asked for a repro; Diego is running a focused test to shorten repro time.

Diego R: Repro procedure I used (short):
1) Start 40 concurrent Gen calls against the same model on node-euw2-14
2) Observe p95/p99 after steady state (~30s)
3) Run vmstat/iostat and capture dmesg

Command: ```hey -n 10000 -c 40 http://node-euw2-14:8080/generate -body '{"prompt":"short"}'```

Maria S: For customer comms: propose temporary mitigation — move affected workloads to dedicated nodes still running driver 525.x in our us-east pool, or temporarily increase concurrency limits. Customer ok with migration?

Ashley M: We should avoid data migration if possible. Prioritize a quick host-level mitigation: drain nodes and roll back the driver on a canary node to 525.85 and validate. If that improves p99, we can do staged rollback and update customers.

Diego R: Rolled back driver on canary node node-euw2-14 -> 525.85 and restarted nvidia-persistenced + inference runtime. Post-rollback numbers: p95 ~230ms and p99 ~760ms — close to baseline. Captured metrics for 10m.

Diego R: ```
# rollback steps (canary)
sudo apt remove --purge nvidia-driver-535
sudo dpkg -i ~/drivers/nvidia-driver-525_525.85_amd64.deb
reboot
# after reboot
systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
```

Tess L: Confirmed: no more Xid messages on canary after rollback. Kernel logs clean. nvme await normalized.

Noah P: NVIDIA support replied: they see a regression with 535.x on some kernels when combined with heavy NVMe IO and large page-faults (SR escalated to engineering). Short-term they recommended either rollback or setting the driver module parameter "NVreg_UsePageRetention=0" (example param) to force a different page-fault path. Haven't fully validated that param here.

Ashley M: OK. Action plan: 1) Roll back drivers on affected nodes (staged, 3 at a time) 2) Notify customers of mitigation and ETA 3) Keep SR open with NVIDIA and share repro harness 4) Add postmortem and long-term mitigation (avoid rolling driver/kernel in same window as capacity-sensitive fleets).

Maria S: I'll draft customer note: explaining root cause as post-maintenance driver/kernel interaction, immediate mitigation (driver rollback), and next steps.

Diego R: Rolling rollback across eu-west pool now — draining nodes one-by-one, replacing drivers, rejoining cluster. Using command: ```redwood-nodectl drain node-euw2-XX && ./driver-rollback.sh node-euw2-XX```

infra-bot: Node node-euw2-15 drained and cordoned by Diego R at 2026-03-10T03:18:45Z

deploy-bot: Canary node-euw2-14 rejoined cluster, runtime health OK, metrics: p99 restored to 0.78s

Noah P: After 6 nodes rolled back, aggregate p99 across eu-west services returned near baseline. Continued monitoring for 24h. NVIDIA engineering acknowledged regression and will produce a patched 535.x build or explicit guidance.

Ashley M: Postmortem TODOs:
- eng-infra: add pre-update compatibility check for driver+kernel combos (automated against small repro harness)
- eng-runtime: add quick-fallback config to cap concurrency on nodes that get updated until validation window passes
- product/support: update runbook for driver/kernel maint windows and customer comms template

Tess L: Filing incident ticket and linking NVIDIA SR. I'll attach logs and timing.

Maria S: Customer updated; they accepted migration/rollback mitigation and appreciate the quick response.

Ashley M: Closing thread once incident ticket and postmortem are attached to the customer escalation. Great triage everyone. :thumbsup:
